description: Figure 6(b) illustrates the impact of the hyperparameter N on the AUC (Area Under the Curve) score, with N ranging from 0 to 20 on the linear x-axis. The y-axis, labeled “AUC (%)”, spans from 75% to 100% in increments of 5%. Five methods are compared, each represented by a distinct colored line with a unique marker: SMD (orange with square markers), PSM (blue with circle markers), SWaT (green with triangle markers), SMAP (purple with diamond markers), and MSL (yellow with diamond markers). As N increases, PSM consistently maintains the highest AUC, peaking near 99% at N=10 before gradually declining to approximately 94% at N=20. SMD and SWaT show similar trends, starting around 85–87%, rising to ~95–96% at N=10, and then slightly decreasing. MSL begins at ~85%, peaks at ~95% at N=10, and declines to ~92% at N=20. SMAP exhibits the most volatile behavior, starting at ~79%, dipping to ~78% at N=5, spiking to ~97% at N=10, then sharply falling to ~85% at N=15 and further to ~82% at N=20.
